pairs.subject: billing-revenue-normalization
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/webhook.rs:1 This context sends job/dataset-change webhooks out and verifies generic HMAC ingress into triggers. It never takes in a billing provider's deliveries as revenue records: a case-insensitive search of crates/server for revenue, invoice, stripe, fx_rate and minor_unit found nothing, so this subject's precondition (a revenue ledger fed by webhooks) does not hold.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/webhook.rs:1231 There is a constant-time HMAC check for inbound ingress, but it protects trigger inputs, not a ledger. This verdict is only about the subject's precondition, not about whether the scheme is sound.
crates/server/src/webhook.rs:6 The delivery log is an outbound DLQ, not records persisted from provider deliveries.

pairs.subject: billing-revenue-normalization
pairs.evidence: crates/core/migrations/0007_cost_ledger.sql:1 The schema has the cost half of unit economics (cost_events in USD) but no revenue table, currency column or FX book: searching crates/core/migrations for revenue, invoice, fx_rate, minor_unit and stripe found nothing, so there are no billing records whose identity, kind, minor units or contract version this subject could govern.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/migrations/0007_cost_ledger.sql:5 Cost events are generated internally, not copies of external billing objects, so a generated id is the technique's own stated non-fit.
crates/core/migrations/0007_cost_ledger.sql:10 Single-currency cost column; there is no multi-currency revenue to convert.
